title: All About Centipedes
checkpoint: Year 1 Spring 1, week 3 — School readiness — Phase 5: new ways to say and spell u, c, g, ch
note_for_grown_ups: Phase 5 continues (School readiness) — non-fiction, real facts about centipedes.

pages.text: Moss spots a bug under the log pile.
pages.illustration: Moss the hedgehog peering under a stack of logs at a small, long, thin brown bug.

pages.text: The bug has a long, thin body.
pages.illustration: A close-up of the long, thin, segmented brown body of the bug under the log.

pages.text: The bug has lots and lots of legs.
pages.illustration: An underside view of the bug showing its many small legs along the length of its body.

pages.text: This kind of bug is a centipede.
pages.illustration: The full centipede resting on a damp log, its long body and many legs clearly visible.

pages.text: A centipede is fast on its legs.
pages.illustration: The centipede darting quickly across the surface of a log.

pages.text: A centipede likes damp, dark spots.
pages.illustration: The centipede tucked into a damp, shadowy gap between two logs.

pages.text: A centipede hides under the log pile.
pages.illustration: The centipede disappearing under the edge of a large log in the log pile.
The centipede close to a tiny bug on the bark of a log.

pages.text: Moss looks as it darts back under the log.
pages.illustration: Moss the hedgehog watching closely as the centipede darts back under a log.

pages.text: Moss is glad the shy bug has a safe home.
pages.illustration: Moss the hedgehog standing contentedly by the log pile, the centipede tucked safely out of sight underneath.
